To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have shown that the S5P CO retrieval algorithm is capable to provide CO column densities for cloudy and clear-sky conditions.
the SCIAMACHYY SICOR CO data set has been improved by the inclusion of cloudy-sky measurements, which more than triple the number of observations.

(i) the SICOR algorithm retrieves CO from clear-sky observations with high accuracy and low noise and that (ii) the SICORE algorithm retrieves CO from cloudy-sky observations with a mean accuracy and noise that is only slightly inferior to the clear-skiy case.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a retrieval algorithm that is able to process SCIAMACHY data and that is ready for the operational data analysis of TROPOMI on S5P.

a comprehensive validation of SCIAMCHY clear-sky and SICOR cloudy-sky CO data sets, where we find an excellent agreement with the validation data sets over oceans and land for clear-sky retrievales and for cloudy-sky retrievaled over the oceans.
the development, validation and application of a new retrieval algorithm for CO vertical column densities from SCIAMACHHY short-wave infrared measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

SICOR provides an accurate retrieval of CO from clear-sky SCIAMACHY measurements over land and from cloudy observations over the oceans and less polluted regions over land, but that the algorithm is not able to capture the strong local CO pollution in urban regions.

the validation results for clear-sky SCIAMACHY CO retrievals over land are in good agreement with the validation results of previous studies, but that for the cloudy-sky retrievers, a validation is only possible for the coastal NDACC and TCCCOn sites.
SICOR is able to retrieve the CO column with a high accuracy of about 10 % in clear-sky and 20 % in cloudy-sky conditions, which is sufficient to meet the requirements of the S5 mission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the S5P CO data processing algorithm is well suited for cloudy observations and that SICOR is ready for the operational processing of S5P CO retrievals.
we provide a full-mission CO data set for clear-sky as well as cloudy-sky measurements from SCIAMACHI, which is a unique data set that will be further extended by TROPOMI measurements in 2017.
the validation shows a high quality of our CO data set and that it is an important addition for CO monitoring and validation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cloudy-sky CO observations are an important complement to clear-sky-only CO data sets and can be processed operationally with the same retrieval algorithm.
the SICOR algorithm can be successfully applied to cloudy observations and provides a valuable data set of CO column amounts for atmospheric research and monitoring applications.
the retrieval of CO from cloudy-sky SCIAMACHY spectra is feasible, but requires a careful validation.
